title: Operator: adaptive rollout FSM with tiered rollback playbook
author: Anika Patel
description: Motivation: rollout behavior for multi-variant model swaps (canaries, A/B, shadow) has grown ad-hoc across controllers. We need a single operator-side finite-state machine that encodes tiered rollout stages, explicit safety lanes (telemetry-driven), and an auditable rollback playbook so on-call and platform engineers can reason about and rehearse safe backouts. This PR adds an adaptive rollout FSM plus a tiered rollback playbook and wiring to the telemetry gate API. Summary: - Introduces a new rollout FSM controller (orchestrator/rollout_fsm) that models stages: dry-shadow -> mini-rehearsal -> staged-canary -> full-swap, with explicit holdpoints and backoff semantics. - Adds a rollback_playbooks directory with prescriptive backout steps and an automated crediting heuristic used by the controller to decide between fast vs staged rollback. - Exposes an operator-facing /api/v1/rollouts/:id/inspect endpoint and a Console inspector to visualize current state, pending holdpoints, and last-triggered rollback reason. - Integrates with telemetry gates: latency, error-rate, model-quality-regressions (via evauls endpoint) and a new SLO budget signal. - Adds integration tests and an e2e dry-rehearsal harness that can replay captured traffic and validate rollback triggers. Checklist: - [x] Design doc: internal doc at /docs/rollouts/adaptive-fsm.md - [x] Unit tests for FSM transitions - [x] Integration tests for telemetry gating - [x] e2e dry-rehearsal recorded run - [x] Console inspector UI and API contract docs - [x] Linear links and rollout playbook committed Related: ENG-2145 (cohort-aware safety lanes), ENG-2190 (rollback creditting RFC). Impact: This refactors several smaller controllers into a single orchestration point; configuration is backwards-compatible (old rollout configs are translated by a compatibility adapter included in this PR). Rollout config examples are added under examples/rollout-configs/tiered-policy.yaml. Notes for reviewers: pay attention to the timing windows for staged-canary (defaults can be tuned via operator config), and the rollback credit algorithm — it's conservative by default to avoid noisy fast-reverts. The description below includes a short commit summary and changed files map.
commits_summary: 3 commits: 1) initial FSM and state machine + basic operator wiring; 2) telemetry gate integration, playbook + tests; 3) console inspector, docs, and fixups after review.
review_conversation: Liam O'Connor (reviewer): The FSM transitions look good; can we make the staged-canary time window configurable per-customer? Also add a test that simulates delayed KV cache flush during swap.
Author (Anika Patel): Good point — added operator config for per-rollout time windows and a unit test (rollout_fsm_test.go) that simulates KV cache delay using the fake-runtime. See commit 2.

Diego Martinez (reviewer): The rollback crediting heuristic seems conservative; would like a knob to allow faster rollback for experimental lanes. Please add a short doc section explaining the economics and safety tradeoffs.

Author: Added 'rollback-credit-policy' config and expanded rollback_playbooks/default_playbook.md with the tradeoffs and recommended defaults. Marked experimental lanes as allowed to be aggressive in the config schema.
Mei Chen (approver): Verified e2e dry rehearsal run locally, inspected metrics emitted (rollout.* metrics), and confirmed console inspector shows holdpoints. Approving after CI green.
CI: initial run failed on tests/integration/rollout_fsm_integration_test.go due to flaky timing; test updated to use jitter-tolerant waits; subsequent CI run passed.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash-and-merge by Mei Chen. Commit message consolidated to: 'orchestrator: add adaptive rollout FSM and tiered rollback playbook (ENG-2145, ENG-2190)'.
release_notes: Introduced adaptive rollout FSM controller + operator API and console inspector; added default rollback playbook and compatibility adapter for legacy rollout configs. Operators can now configure tiered canaries, dry-rehearsals, and rollback-credit policies.
